SOURCE: "MASS-RAG: Multi-Agent Synthesis Retrieval-Augmented Generation", Xingchen Xiao, Heyan Huang, Runheng Liu (Beijing Institute of Technology) and Jincheng Xie (Tsinghua). arXiv:2604.18509v2 [cs.CL], 21 Apr 2026. Preprint. The layout looks like an ACL-style submission, but no venue is printed.

COVERAGE: All 19 pages and 62,237 chars. This covers the main text, limitations, references (skimmed), and appendices A to E. Case studies D (Figures 5 to 10) were read through Case Study 4. The rest of the case-study text was not read, because it only illustrates cases. Figure 3 is a bar chart, so its values are not in the extracted text.

CLAIMS
(ranked by importance)

- claim: MASS-RAG is a training-free pipeline of three filter agents (Summarizer, Extractor, Reasoner), an optional Answer Agent, and a Synthesis Agent. It beats single-judge-filter MAIN-RAG and trained Self-RAG on most of the four tasks.
  number: See the Table 1 rows below.
  setup: Zero-shot and greedy (temperature 0, top-p 1.0). Retrieval is the Self-RAG release: up to 20 passages ranked by Contriever (MS MARCO). Top-5 passages are used for Llama2 7B and top-10 for the other models. Benchmarks are TriviaQA, PopQA (1,399 long-tail questions), ARC-Challenge (1,172 test questions) and ASQA (948 questions).
  quote: "MASS-RAG-Llama3 8B 76.7 64.2 78.7 47 35.2 55.2" and "MAIN-RAG-Llama3∗8B 74.1 64.0 61.9 39.2 42.0 70.6"
  where: Table 1, p.5
  Table 1 columns are TriviaQA acc, PopQA acc, ARC-C acc, ASQA em, rg, mau. Other rows:
  - Self-RAG 7B: 66.4, 54.9, 67.3, 30.0, 35.7, 74.3
  - MASS-RAG-Llama2 7B: 68.6, 57.8, 72.2, 36.2, 33.3, 20.94
  - MASS-RAG-Mistral 7B: 73.7, 60.9, 72.4, 41.6, 37.1, 69.8
  - MASS-RAG-Qwen3 8B: 74.1, 63.9, 87.3, 47.5, 37.4, 53.5
  - Qwen3 8B plain RAG: 72, 62.1, 86.4, 46.1, 35.7, 16.1

- claim: The paper's "absolute" gains are actually relative percentages. For example, 2.2 points over 66.4 is 3.3%, and 16.8 points over 61.9 is 27.1%. This is my arithmetic from Table 1, not the paper's statement. Cite the raw points, not the quoted percentages.
  number: Self-RAG comparison, 3.3%, 5.3%, 7.3%, 20.7%. MAIN-RAG comparison, 3.5%, 0.3%, 27.1%, 19.9%.
  setup: Self-RAG comparison uses Llama2 7B. MAIN-RAG comparison uses Llama3 8B.
  quote: "MASS-RAG achieves absolute accuracy improvements of up to 3.3%, 5.3%, 7.3%, and 20.7% on the four selected tasks" and "MASS-RAG yields improvements of up to 3.5%, 0.3%, 27.1%, and 19.9% across the same tasks"
  where: Section 4.3, p.6
  Raw point gaps over MAIN-RAG with Llama3 8B: TriviaQA +2.6, PopQA +0.2, ARC-C +16.8, ASQA-em +7.8.

- claim: MASS-RAG is weak or mixed on some metrics. MAIN-RAG-Llama3 is higher on ASQA ROUGE and MAUVE. Self-RAG is higher on ASQA MAUVE. MASS-RAG-Llama2 has a low MAUVE of 20.94. MAIN-RAG's PopQA (64.0) is essentially tied with MASS-RAG-Llama3 (64.2).
  number: ROUGE 42.0 against 35.2. MAUVE 70.6 against 55.2.
  setup: ASQA, Llama3 8B.
  quote: "MAIN-RAG-Llama3∗8B 74.1 64.0 61.9 39.242.070.6"
  where: Table 1, p.5

- claim: The ARC-Challenge gain over MAIN-RAG is large. The paper does not control for the fact that the Qwen3 8B baseline with plain RAG already scores 86.4.
  number: ARC-C 78.7 for MASS-RAG-Llama3, 61.9 for MAIN-RAG-Llama3, and 87.3 for MASS-RAG-Qwen3 against 86.4 for Qwen3 plain RAG.
  setup: Table 1, ARC-C, answer agent disabled.
  quote: "Qwen38B 72 62.1 86.4 46.1 35.7 16.1"
  where: p.5

- claim: The gains hold at a shallower retrieval depth. With 5 documents, MASS-RAG-Llama3 reaches TriviaQA 75.8, PopQA 61.5, ARC-C 79.9 and ASQA 45.2. The paper says it outperforms MAIN-RAG on TriviaQA, ARC-C and ASQA at the shallower depth.
  number: Depth 5 and depth 10, Table 2.
  setup: Llama3 8B and Mistral 7B. The MAIN-RAG row is the 10-document run only.
  quote: "MASS-RAG(Llama38B) 75.8 61.5 79.9 45.2" and "MAIN-RAG(Llama38B) 74.1 64.0 61.9 39.2"
  where: Table 2, p.6
  The "stable trends" wording is the authors' own summary.

- claim: The Answer Agent helps factoid QA and does not help long-form QA. Without it, TriviaQA with Mistral drops from 77.5 to 76.0. On ASQA, dropping it improves the score.
  number: See the quote for Table 3. ASQA moves from 41.6 to 43.9 (Mistral) and from 47.0 to 48.0 (Llama3). PopQA with Mistral goes from 60.9 to 61.9 without the Answer Agent, which is the opposite direction.
  setup: Mistral 7B and Llama3 8B, top-10 documents.
  quote: "TriviaQA Mistral77.576.0Llama379.979.3" and "ASQA Mistral 41.643.9Llama3 47.048.0"
  where: Table 3, p.7
  The text claims a consistent PopQA gain, but PopQA-Mistral contradicts it: the text says "incorporating the Answer Agent consistently improves performance on factoid QA benchmarks". The extracted Table 3 also shows TriviaQA 77.5 for Mistral, while Table 1 gives 73.7, so the two tables do not agree. Flag as a table inconsistency.

- claim: The filter agents catch different evidence. On the Uniquely Attributable Subset, each filter agent covers questions the others miss. Intermediate filter outputs often score higher than the final synthesised answer.
  number: Subset sizes are 609 and 108 for Llama3 (TriviaQA, PopQA), and 559 and 85 for Mistral. See the Table 4 quote.
  setup: Top-10 documents. The subset keeps only questions whose gold evidence is captured by exactly one filter agent.
  quote: "Summarizer 73.7 65.7 ... Synthesis 76.7 64.2" (Llama3 8B, Table 4) and "Reasoner 71.9 62.4 ... Synthesis 73.6 60.9" (Mistral 7B, Table 5)
  where: Tables 4 and 5, p.8
  On PopQA the Summarizer alone (65.7) and the Reasoner alone (Mistral, 62.4) beat the synthesis step. The synthesis step wins clearly only on TriviaQA with Llama3. The Extractor is the weakest agent everywhere. The authors say the filtered responses "can be viewed as an approximate upper bound", and that stronger backbones (Llama3 over Mistral) get closer to it.

- claim: The cost is 7 agent calls per sample with the Answer Agent and 4 without.
  number: 7x and 4x.
  setup: The paper assumes 100 tokens per call. This is an analytical estimate, not a measurement.
  quote: "MASS-RAG w/ Answer Agent 7x MASS-RAG w/o Answer Agent 4x"
  where: Table 7, Appendix E, p.13
  Latency, dollar cost and token cost are not measured.

- claim: Task fit differs. The Answer Agent is off for multiple-choice ARC-C, because option labels carry little semantic content, and it is a mixed bet for long-form ASQA.
  number: none
  setup: Section 4.4.
  quote: "for multiple-choice tasks with symbolic option labels (e.g., A/B/C/D), intermediate candidate answers provide limited additional signal"
  where: p.4

LIMITS
- The authors concede that the retriever, reranker and decoding are held fixed. They test no learned or adaptive components. They say the design is "amenable to future extensions".
- Every number comes from a single retriever's pre-computed passages from Self-RAG's release. No fresh retrieval and no hybrid search were tried. There are no seeds, variances or significance tests.
- Baselines marked "∗" are copied from other papers, not re-run. Only Qwen3 and the MASS-RAG rows are the authors' runs.
- Models are 7B to 8B only, with Llama2 13B as a baseline. Tasks are short-form QA, multiple-choice and one long-form set. There is no multi-hop dataset such as HotpotQA, no enterprise data and no long documents.
- Role prompts are not given verbatim. Only prose descriptions appear in Appendix C.
- Runtime is analytical, not measured. There is no comparison to a single stronger call, such as one reasoning call or one reranker, at equal compute.
- The tables disagree in places (see the Table 3 note), and the percentages are mislabelled as "absolute" (see above).
- The paper has no failure analysis. The ethics statement says the system does not guarantee correctness.

BUILDS ON
- MAIN-RAG, Chang et al. 2024: the single judge agent that scores and filters documents, and the main baseline.
- Self-RAG, Asai et al. 2023: the retrieval release, the benchmarks and the training-based baseline.
- RECOMP, Xu et al. 2023, and DSLR, Hwang et al. 2024: summarising or compressing the context.
- Extractive QA, Chen et al. 2017, and Lewis et al. 2021: the Extractor's design.
- Reranking, Glass et al. 2022 (Re2G): the standard way to filter context.
- Query rewriting, Ma et al. 2023 and RQ-RAG (Chan et al. 2024): another context-refinement route.
- Context filtering, Wang et al. 2023b, and PRCA (Yang et al. 2023): learned filters.
- Multi-agent RAG, MA-RAG (Nguyen et al. 2025) and MMOA-RAG (Chen et al. 2025).
- Lost in the middle, Liu et al. 2023: motivation for noisy context.
- Metric: Evidence Coverage Rate, "inspired by" Answer Inclusion Rate (Ruan et al. 2024).
- Contriever, Izacard et al. 2022a: the retriever.

CODE: None. No pseudocode, and the prompts are not reproduced. Equations 1 to 6 describe the pipeline as Summarizer, Extractor and Reasoner outputs R(s), R(e), R(r), then optional candidate answers A(j) = A_ans(q, R(j)), then Ŷ = A_syn(q, {A(s), A(e), A(r)}), or A_syn(q, {R(s), R(e), R(r)}) when the Answer Agent is off (p.3 to 4).

FIGURES
- Figure 1 (p.1): a single filter-judge agent against the multi-agent filter plus synthesis. This is the quickest picture of the idea.
- Figure 2 (p.3): the architecture, from retriever to the three filter agents, the optional Answer Agent producing three candidates, then Synthesis.
- Figure 3 (p.8): bar chart of the Evidence Coverage Rate per agent on the Uniquely Attributable Subset. The values are not in the text and need the image.
- Figure 4 (p.13): bar comparison against Self-RAG and MAIN-RAG.
- Figures 5 to 10 (pp.14 to 19): case studies. Figures 5 and 6 (PopQA, Mistral) show a single agent finding the evidence and the Synthesis Agent recovering the right answer.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions were found.
- The text extraction is clean, except that Table 1 bold and underline marks run numbers together (for example "35.774.3" and "47.5137.4").
- Tables 1 and 3 disagree (see the Table 3 note).
